solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Oppose this means of execution

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to go against or contradict someone
second meaning: the wooden frame used for crucifixion

explanation.surface: A campaigner urges us to stand against a particular form of capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one protest against a method of killing; the verb and the noun are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart someone is a verb sense of the word, and crucifixion was carried out on a wooden upright with a crossbeam.

clue.text: Nonsense about rat getting to kill monster

parts.note: cock is slang for rubbish talk, as in poppycock

indicators.note: turned about suggests the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
to ice someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: Talk of a rodent going on to slay a beast is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatrice is a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg, whose gaze could kill — a fabulous monster.

clue.text: Fly without second propeller

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An aircraft takes off without its backup propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar drives a rowing boat through the water, so it propels the craft.

clue.text: Nobleman almost trapped by artful character in Dickens

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside something else

parts.note: sly means cunning, artful

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an earl is a peer

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is very nearly caught by the Artful Dodger in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artful character in Dickens' suggests the Artful Dodger, but 'artful' is a plain synonym. Mr Sleary runs the circus in Hard Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleary is the lisping circus proprietor in Dickens's novel Hard Times, a figure from his fiction.

clue.text: Peter's lad managed to get drunk

indicators.note: to manage something is to handle and arrange it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Peter's son found a way to get himself thoroughly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is informal slang for heavily intoxicated, an adjective like the definition.

clue.text: Knight pursues woman belonging to the aristocracy

indicators.note: one who pursues follows behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a woman's name
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight chases a noblewoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricians were the hereditary noble class of ancient Rome, so the adjective means aristocratic.

clue.text: Earl taking time over packing good suit

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards
packing something means holding it inside

parts.note: an era is a period of time
G is the abbreviation for good
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A nobleman takes his time packing a decent outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing, but it is the verb: to be agreeable to.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, 'suit' means to be acceptable or right for, as in 'spicy food doesn't agree with me'.

clue.text: A number outside object to extremely creepy political faction

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: ten is a number
an end is an aim or object

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A crowd lodges an objection to an unpleasantly sinister political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a verb but is the noun, a goal; Militant Tendency was a Trotskyist group in the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a group within a party holding distinct views, as with the Militant Tendency.

clue.text: It is sung to create trouble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1974 disco hit by the Hues Corporation
second meaning: an idiom for upsetting a settled situation

explanation.surface: A song is performed to stir up a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sentence about a song's purpose; the song title and the idiom are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for disturbing a stable situation, and also the title of a well-known pop record.

clue.text: Died up river in action

parts.note: d. is the abbreviation for died

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone was killed in fighting upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act or something done, so it is a synonym for action.

clue.text: What Jesus was to find fault with is on record

parts.note: to carp is to complain pettily
to enter something in a ledger is to record it

explanation.surface: A sceptic, it seems, sets out on the record to pick holes in Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a theological argument; the definition is simply Jesus's trade before his ministry, as Joseph's son.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospels describe Jesus as a woodworker's son who followed the same trade, a joiner in wood.

clue.text: Heroin entering French port is aimed at a small specialised market

definitions.text: aimed at a small specialised market

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it

parts.note: Nice is a port on the French Riviera
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Drugs smuggled into a Riviera harbour serve only a limited clientele.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, as in 'a niche product', it describes goods targeted at a narrow segment of buyers.

clue.text: Notice hesitation at various times during arrival

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls inside its span

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
er is the sound of hesitating

indicators.note: various suggests things in assorted forms, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices a repeated dithering whenever a newcomer turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The hesitation and the jumbled times together sit inside the arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a public announcement or posted bill, which is what an advertisement is.

clue.text: Very close to Mark in defence

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
a mark is a sign or indication

explanation.surface: A defender stands very near Mark in the back line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like part of the wordplay's meaning, but it only places the abbreviation next to the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindication is a justification of a person or claim against criticism, which is a defence.

clue.text: Abandoned dairy beyond Nice destroyed by nationalist bomb

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and uncontrolled, so the letters are let loose

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for nationalist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disused farm building outside Nice has been blown up by a separatist's bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' places the rearranged dairy after the rearranged Nice-plus-nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: An incendiary is a device designed to start fires, a fire bomb.

clue.text: Largely opposed after Republican's bombast

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
anti means against

explanation.surface: A Republican's overblown speech was mostly against everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after Republican's' places the shortened word for opposed after the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated speech, and a rant is a loud, overblown tirade.

clue.text: Get rid of cover from protective shield

parts.note: to fire an employee is to get rid of them
a screen shelters or covers something

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take the cover off a protective shield.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a guard placed in front of a hearth to protect the room from sparks.

clue.text: Portrayal of girl with hint of trepidation facing fellows in court

indicators.note: being in a place means standing within its walls, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name
CT is the abbreviation for court

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter
men are fellows

explanation.surface: An anxious girl faces a group of men in a courtroom, and someone paints the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is a performance or acting out of a role, so it is a portrayal.

clue.text: One willing to examine a bull's back

parts.note: to test is to examine
taken as written

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: A vet is happy to look over the rear of a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One willing' reads as eager, but it means someone making a will; 'bull's back' looks anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so a punning description is someone who wills their estate.

clue.text: Conflict caused by Sadat after an illegal act

indicators.note: after means following, so the piece before this word is placed second

parts.note: a crime is an act against the law
Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt

explanation.surface: A Middle East war is blamed on the Egyptian president following some lawless deed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadat stands for his first name; the war he suggests is not the answer, which is the 1850s conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1853–56 fight between Russia and an alliance including Britain and France was a war, a conflict.

clue.text: Revolted by Bush

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shrub bearing thorny stems and fragrant flowers

explanation.surface: Someone was disgusted by the American president Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the president, and revolted like disgust; both are separate meanings of a four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebels rise up, so a past-tense rising is a revolt; the flower grows on a thorny shrub.

clue.text: Not entirely correct over copper's sharpness

indicators.note: lying over something in a down clue means covering it, so it encloses
not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to amend is to correct
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman's wits are not quite up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper's' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; the 's is a link meaning 'has' or 'gives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keenness of judgement, mental sharpness in business or practical matters.

clue.text: Note found in haunted attic surprisingly proved to be genuine

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: E is a musical note
the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A letter discovered in a spooky loft is, against expectations, shown to be real.
explanation.definitionFit: To authenticate a document is to establish that it is real, so the past participle means verified as real.

clue.text: One presiding over an event in the centre of Bremen getting caught with drugs

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the middle two letters of a six-letter word
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
E is ecstasy, so two of them

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies in a German city is arrested in possession of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Bremen is a German city; the definition is the long opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee, from MC, is the master of ceremonies who hosts a show or formal event.

clue.text: Niece oddly neglected to go after an award for style

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

indicators.note: neglecting the odd letters leaves only the even-numbered ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A niece is strangely overlooked when an award for style goes to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic as a noun means elegance and stylishness, a synonym for style.

clue.text: Poins introduced to TV presenter in lift

indicators.note: being introduced to something here means being put inside it

parts.note: a host presents a television show
Poins is this puzzle's setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter meets a television presenter while riding in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; Poins here gives the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for raising loads, equivalent to the noun lift.

clue.text: Best thereupon starts to demolish another drink

parts.note: the cream is the best part
so means accordingly, thereupon

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Having drunk the best stuff, a drinker sets about finishing off one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' looks like it belongs to the definition, but only its first letter is wanted; the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured fizzy soft drink, a carbonated beverage.

clue.text: Be indebted to a passage from Powell

indicators.note: a passage from a text is an extract taken from within it

parts.note: the second to fourth letters of this name

explanation.surface: A writer acknowledges a debt to a quotation from Powell.
explanation.walkthrough: Powell could be the novelist Anthony Powell or the politician Enoch Powell; the name is just a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe someone is to be under an obligation, in debt to them.

clue.text: Corresponding with Italian fellow about game

parts.note: con is the Italian word for with

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a gent is a man, a fellow
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: An Italian man exchanges letters with a chap about a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding with' looks like letter-writing, but 'with Italian' is the Italian preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruent means in agreement or matching, so it is a synonym of corresponding in the sense of tallying.

clue.text: Poor newspaper boss without money in retirement? Just the opposite

indicators.note: without means outside, the surrounding position
this phrase swaps the roles, so the piece said to be outside goes inside instead
retiring means going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: the yen is Japan's currency
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor who has retired penniless is hard up — or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the editor goes round the money; 'Just the opposite' tells you to put the turned-round money round the editor instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy describes people lacking the necessities of life, just as poor does.
